text.p: Tengasco Inc said Wednesday it is challenging the legality of warrants attached to three 1996 loans.
The company said it does not dispute its indebtedness to the three lenders, but it does dispute the terms of the agreements relating to the debt.

In October and November, Tengasco said, it borrowed $250,000, $250,000 and $500,000 from Ulrich Hocker, an individual residing outside the United States, Thieme Fonds, a Luxembourg company, and Wallington Investments Ltd, a Swiss corporation, respectively.
Each borrowing was for a six-month term and at an interest rate of 10 percent per annum. The debts become due in April and May 1997.
At the time of the borrowings, a spokesman said, tghe company verbally agreed to issue warrants along with the debt.

However, an officer no longer with the company signed off on warrant agreement containing what the company called "materially harsh anti-dilution provisions which purportedly become effective upon certain events and circumstances to lower the exercise price per share."
The spokesman said these terms were never approved by the company's board.
He said the company expects to negotiate a settlement with the lenders.

Tengasco said its directors, while acknowledging the debt to the three lenders, has rejected the terms of the written agreements reflecting the loans, as well as the terms of the warrant agreements, explaining the board views the terms of the agreements as not being properly authorized.
On December 26, Thieme Fonds gave notice to Tengasco of exercise of warrants to purchase 28,818 shares of Tengasco at $3.53 per share.
Pending resolution of the controversy, Tengasco said, it has not accepted Thieme Fonds' exercise of the warrant by issuing Tengasco common stock.
